lens: Reversibility — revert cost, data loss, rollback runbook
answer: git revert 59534679 restores all 24 changed files cleanly. The PR is pure deletion of stateless Rust source and docs — no database migrations, no deployed artifacts, no external system writes. Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock membership entries are restored by the revert, making the workspace buildable again in one step. ADR-0118 does NOT have a dedicated '## Rollback / Reversal' section; the only revert guidance is a one-liner in IP-008's Done-criteria ('Revert the retirement PR with plain git if downstream history proves the one-time archive payload is still required'). That is marginally sufficient for a pure-deletion lane retirement but falls short of the runbook standard set by prior ADRs. If the lane needs to come back, git revert is unambiguously the simpler path — there is no state to reconcile and no migration to reverse. Rebuilding from scratch would require re-authoring ~700 lines of Rust plus re-adding workspace members and catalog entries. Cost class: cheap revert.
key_claims: git revert 59534679 restores all 24 files atomically — pure deletion means the inverse patch applies without conflict
No stateful migration occurred: no DB rows, no deployed binaries, no external system writes — data_loss_class = none
Cargo workspace membership is restored by the revert; a single 'cargo check' confirms re-inclusion
ADR-0118 has no '## Rollback / Reversal' section; revert guidance exists only as a single sentence in IP-008 Done-criteria
Simpler revert path is git revert, not rebuild; rebuild would require re-authoring ~700 lines of Rust plus catalog/workspace entries
uncertainty_areas: Whether any downstream branch (e.g. oya-m01-m02-gate-usecase-doc-drift, which is the current branch) has already built on the assumption that the archive-orphan packages are absent — a revert would re-introduce them and could cause duplicate-member conflicts if a branch independently re-declared them

The pre-grit archive payload (bominal/agents/ultragoal/archive/pre-grit-cutover-2026-05-12/) is deleted; git revert restores the README.md but the rest of that directory's contents (if any files beyond README.md existed) are recoverable only if they were tracked before the merge
revert_steps: 1. git revert 59534679 --no-edit  — restores all 24 files; no manual conflict resolution expected for a pure-deletion revert
2. ~/.rustup/toolchains/1.95.0-aarch64-apple-darwin/bin/cargo metadata --no-deps --format-version 1 | grep archive-orphan — confirm both packages re-appear
4. Verify registry catalog entries restored: ls registry/catalog/oya-foundry-fitness-archive-orphan*.yaml — expect 3 files
5. Open a follow-up PR against dev with the revert commit; do not push directly to dev without review

findings.summary: ADR-0118 lacks a '## Rollback / Reversal' section. A one-line revert hint in IP-008 Done-criteria is present but not surfaced in the ADR itself, which is the canonical decision record future maintainers will consult.
findings.recommended_action: Add a '## Rollback / Reversal' section to ADR-0118 citing 'git revert 59534679' as the recovery command and noting the cargo metadata verification step. Docs-only fixup, no code change.
